| **Property & fuzz** | [`property_test`](../../tests/property_test.rs), [`smoke_fuzz_test`](../../tests/smoke_fuzz_test.rs), [`fuzz_corpus_replay`](../../tests/fuzz_corpus_replay.rs) | `proptest` invariants; the always-on stable-toolchain fuzz floor; and — despite its name — a deterministic sweep over an adversarial seed set defined *in the file itself*, not a replay of [`fuzz/corpus/`](../../fuzz/corpus/) (it opens no files). |
| **Contract** | [`json_schema_test`](../../tests/json_schema_test.rs), [`summary_consistency_test`](../../tests/summary_consistency_test.rs), [`output_behavior_test`](../../tests/output_behavior_test.rs), [`error_types_test`](../../tests/error_types_test.rs), [`api_guidelines_test`](../../tests/api_guidelines_test.rs), [`wasm_exports_test`](../../tests/wasm_exports_test.rs) | The shapes other people's code depends on: JSON schemas, cross-surface summary agreement, machine-readable output flags, typed errors, `#[non_exhaustive]` on growth-prone enums, WASM export list. |

| **Meta** | [`support_selftest`](../../tests/support_selftest.rs) | The shared test helpers have their own tests. |

## [`tests/support/`](../../tests/support/)

Files in a subdirectory of `tests/` are **not** compiled as their own test
binaries. So an explicit path attribute pulls shared helpers in:

```rust
#[path = "support/run.rs"]
mod run;
```

That idiom is why the same module appears in several test files
with no `mod.rs` chain. Each test binary compiles its own copy.

| Helper | Provides |
|---|---|
| [`mod.rs`](../../tests/support/mod.rs) | Shared normalization (`normalize()`) used to compare output across platforms; self-tested by `support_selftest`. |
| [`run.rs`](../../tests/support/run.rs) | The canonical binary-spawn helper for CLI/output/config integration tests — one place that knows how to find and invoke the built binary. |
| [`server.rs`](../../tests/support/server.rs) | REST API spawn harness: start the server on an ephemeral port, wait for readiness, tear down. |
| [`mcp.rs`](../../tests/support/mcp.rs) | The same for HTTP MCP, including the JSON-RPC framing. |
| [`teardown.rs`](../../tests/support/teardown.rs) | `terminate()`, the one way a harness stops the binary it spawned: SIGTERM, a bounded wait, and SIGKILL only for a child still running after it. `Child::kill()` is SIGKILL, and a process killed that way never writes its coverage profile. Pulled in with `include!` rather than `#[path]`. |
| [`schema.rs`](../../tests/support/schema.rs) | JSON-Schema validation against [`tests/schemas/`](../../tests/schemas). |
| [`tui_fixtures.rs`](../../tests/support/tui_fixtures.rs) | SIP fixture builders shared by the TUI snapshot and state tests. |
| [`executable.rs`](../../tests/support/executable.rs) | `write_executable()`, the one way a test writes a file it then runs: a child process writes it, so this process never holds it open for writing and an `exec` cannot fail with `ETXTBSY` ("Text file busy") while another test thread forks. `executable_stub_test` refuses a file written in-process and then made executable. |
| [`fuzz.rs`](../../tests/support/fuzz.rs) | A deterministic xorshift PRNG shared by the stable-toolchain fuzzers, so a failure reproduces from its seed. |
| [`ports.rs`](../../tests/support/ports.rs) | `refused_tcp_port()`, the one way a test gets a loopback TCP port where a connect fails with `ConnectionRefused`: a socket bound and not listening, held until the guard drops, so no test running alongside can bind the number. Binding `:0`, reading the port, and closing the socket leaves the number free for another test to listen on; `released_port_scan_test` refuses that pattern under `tests/`. |

## Fixtures and corpora

Every command below ran against the current tree and left it unchanged.

- That is the point of documenting them.
- If one produces a diff, something has drifted.

| Artifact | Regenerate with |
|---|---|
| [`tests/fixtures/`](../../tests/fixtures) — capture fixtures | Every capture in the directory comes from [`tests/support/synthetic_captures.rs`](../../tests/support/synthetic_captures.rs), and so do the two SIPp media files in `harness/sipp/scenarios/` and the two fuzz seeds in `fuzz/corpus/pcap_reader/` named `truncated-sip` and `empty-classic`: seventeen in all. `cargo run --features native --bin gen_fixture` writes them, relative to the `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` Cargo sets (the current directory when run outside Cargo), and `synthetic_captures_test` fails when a committed byte differs from what the generator builds. The directory's other fixtures, the JSON goldens, `ng` replies and TLS keys, stay as checked in. [`tests/PROVENANCE.md`](../../tests/PROVENANCE.md) records where every capture outside `tests/pcap-samples/` came from, and `every_committed_capture_is_public_or_synthetic` refuses one with no entry, finding captures by their leading bytes rather than their names. |
| [`tests/snapshots/`](../../tests/snapshots) — TUI buffers | `cargo insta test --features tui --accept` (needs `cargo install cargo-insta`) |
| [`tests/cli/`](../../tests/cli) — trycmd goldens | `TRYCMD=overwrite cargo test --features full --test cli_goldens` |
| [`tests/cli/cookbook/`](../../tests/cli/cookbook) — cookbook output goldens | `python3 scripts/check-cookbook.py --bless` writes a command-only case for each executed cookbook command that has none and deletes each case no command produces; then `TRYCMD=overwrite cargo test --features full --test cli_goldens` records the output. A case's file name is a hash of its command, and it is also the directory the command's output files go to. |
| [`tests/schemas/`](../../tests/schemas) — JSON Schemas | Hand-maintained; `json_schema_test` validates output against them. |
| [`tests/pcap-samples/`](../../tests/pcap-samples) — capture fixtures | Thirteen are synthetic: `python3 tests/gen-pcap-samples.py` writes ten and `python3 tests/gen-link-type-samples.py` writes the three link-layer framings (DLT_LOOP, PPPoE inside Linux cooked capture v1 and v2); each script in check mode reports any of its own that have drifted from it. Nothing regenerates the rest; they stay as checked in. New ones arrive through [`harness/scripts/capture.sh`](../../harness/scripts/capture.sh) then `promote.sh`, which record the run in `PROVENANCE.md` beside them — `every_committed_capture_fixture_says_where_it_came_from` refuses a fixture with no entry, and the 36 that predate that rule sit on an enumerated list which only shrinks. |
| [`tests/install-sh/`](../../tests/install-sh) — installer cases | Hand-maintained; exercised by the `install-sh` CI job. |
| [`fuzz/corpus/`](../../fuzz/corpus) — fuzz seeds | Grown by `cargo fuzz run` (nightly). Note nothing on the stable toolchain reads this directory: `fuzz_corpus_replay` drives its own in-file seed set. To make a reproducer run in every `cargo test`, add it to `smoke_fuzz_test` as well. |

### The public vCon datasets

The vcon-dev community publishes five vCon datasets as git repositories.

- They hold 17,443 containers in all.
- None of them carries SIP signaling.
- [`tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/PINS.tsv`](../../tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/PINS.tsv)
  pins each one to a commit.
  - It records the license of its LICENSE file at that commit.

Two tests read them.

- [`vcon_dataset_subset_test`](../../tests/vcon_dataset_subset_test.rs) runs on
  every build with the `vcon` feature.
  - It reads the four containers committed
    under [`tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/`](../../tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/README.md).
  - It pins the findings `vcon_schema::validate` reports for each.
  - It also checks three more things:
    - The `jsonschema` reference engine agrees.
    - Each container is valid once the test repairs its recorded dataset issues.
    - The fetcher (`--vcon-fetch-kind generic`, against a server on `127.0.0.1`)
      saves each one unchanged.
  - Each dataset directory there carries the LICENSE file of its dataset.
  - It also carries a README with the source path and SHA-256 of every file.
- [`vcon_dataset_corpus_test`](../../tests/vcon_dataset_corpus_test.rs) reads
  every container in the five datasets.
  - It runs only when `SIPNAB_VCON_DATASETS` names a directory that
    [`scripts/fetch-vcon-datasets.py`](../../scripts/fetch-vcon-datasets.py)
    filled.
  - Without it, the binary prints one `NOTICE` line saying its gates did
    not run, as the capture corpus does.
  - The pre-push corpus gate does not run it.
    That gate selects tests by the name `SIPNAB_CORPUS`.

Fetch the datasets and run the corpus test:

```sh
# Run all of these, in order.
python3 scripts/fetch-vcon-datasets.py "$HOME/vcon-datasets"
SIPNAB_VCON_DATASETS="$HOME/vcon-datasets" \
  cargo test --features full --profile corpus --test vcon_dataset_corpus_test
```

The script runs only `git`.

- It fetches each pinned commit.
- It checks it out detached, with hooks and symbolic links turned off.
- It refuses a checkout whose HEAD is not the pinned commit.
- It refuses a checkout whose files have changed.
- A second run verifies the cache and moves a dataset whose pin changed.
- The five datasets take about 2.3 GB of disk.
- The corrected copy described below takes about 2.2 GB more.

The corpus test prints three things for each dataset:

- The number of containers.
- The number the schema accepts.
- Each finding, with the number of containers that carry it.

It asserts these things:

- Each dataset is at its pinned commit.
- sipnab and the reference agree on every container.
  - They agree on the verdict.
  - They agree on the instance paths of the findings.
- The per-dataset counts measured on 2026-10-09.
  - These hold for as long as the pins do.
  - Moving a pin in `PINS.tsv` means measuring again and rewriting `EXPECTED` in the test.

What the five datasets get, at their pins:

| Dataset | Containers | Valid | Findings, with the number of containers that carry each |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vcon-supreme-court-arguments` | 8,503 | 0 | Attachment Object without `mediatype`: 8,503 |
| `ietf-meeting-vcons` | 8,181 | 0 | Attachment Object without `mediatype`: 8,181. Dialog Object with `url` and no `content_hash`: 4,079 |
| `vcon-dataset-city-of-newport-ri` | 115 | 0 | Attachment Object without `mediatype`: 115. Dialog Object with `url` and no `content_hash`: 115 |
| `fake-vcons` | 601 | 0 | Attachment Object without `mediatype`: 601. Attachment Object without `start`: 601. Dialog Object with a `body` and no `encoding`: 264 |
| `tadhack-2025` | 43 | 0 | Attachment Object without `mediatype`: 43. Attachment Object without `start`: 43 |

Each finding is a rule that draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 states in its prose
and in its schema:

- [section 4.4.5](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.4.5)
  for an inline attachment's `mediatype`.
- [section 4.4.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.4.2)
  for `start`.
- [section 2.4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-2.4)
  for `content_hash` beside `url`.
- [section 2.3.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-2.3.2)
  for `encoding`.

The reference engine reports the same findings at the same paths.
With those four repaired, every one of the 17,443 containers is valid
to sipnab and to the reference engine.

#### The corrected copy

[`tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/CORRECTED.tsv`](../../tests/fixtures/vcon-datasets/CORRECTED.tsv)
pins [NormB/vcon-datasets-core04](https://github.com/NormB/vcon-datasets-core04).

- It is a copy of the first three datasets.
- It adds two kinds of key and changes nothing else:
  - `mediatype` on every inline attachment.
  - `content_hash` on the 425 IETF audio recordings whose files it downloaded,
    with an IETF login, and hashed.
- Its CHANGES.md lists what it leaves open and why.
- fake-vcons and tadhack-2025 are not in it.
  - The reason is the contact data described in the subset README.
- The fetch script fetches both pins files unless `--pins` names others.
- It accepts `--pins` more than once.

The corpus test holds the corrected copy to three things.
These are beside the tests above that pin the upstream findings.

- It is at its pinned commit.
- Each corrected dataset gets the answer measured on 2026-10-11.
  - sipnab and the reference agree on every container.
- Each corrected container is its upstream container with keys added.
  - The test counts the added `content_hash` values (425).
  - It requires each to be a SHA-512 token.
  - With them set aside, repairing both containers with the test's own repair
    gives the same document.
  - The corrected one needs no `mediatype` repair.
  - That last check compares this repository's repair rule with the
    corrected repository's own, on all 16,799 containers.

| Dataset | Containers | Valid | Findings, with the number of containers that carry each |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vcon-supreme-court-arguments` | 8,503 | 8,503 | None |
| `ietf-meeting-vcons` | 8,181 | 4,527 | Dialog Object with `url` and no `content_hash`: 3,654 |
| `vcon-dataset-city-of-newport-ri` | 115 | 0 | Dialog Object with `url` and no `content_hash`: 115 |

The remaining finding needs a hash of each recording.
No fetch returns these recordings to hash.

- The IETF ones are YouTube pages.
- The Newport video host refused the download.

Accepting a snapshot or overwriting a golden is a **decision**, not a fix.

- Read the diff first.
- These files are the record of what the tool promised its users.

## The gate-test roster

These fail on changes you thought had nothing to do with them.
Each one exists because the thing it guards silently rotted at least once.

| Gate | Trips when |
|---|---|
| [`docs_drift_test`](../../tests/docs_drift_test.rs) | A `--flag` named on a published page does not exist in the CLI. That corpus derives from `git ls-files` rather than a hand-kept list, and covers every tracked `docs/` page except `design/` and `research/`, plus `website/content/`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` — these pages included, so a phantom flag here fails too. A flag belonging to another tool goes in `FOREIGN_FLAGS`, scoped to the label of each page naming it. Also: a version marker in the docs or man page disagrees with `Cargo.toml`; the README feature table misses a Cargo feature; a `[theme]` slot in `ThemeConfig` has no documentation, or the slot count quoted in either config reference is wrong. Also the benchmark reproducibility contract: the `bench/` harness the benchmarks page tells readers to run must exist and be executable, [`bench/carrier.py`](../../bench/carrier.py) must still produce the corpus composition the page quotes (checked at 1/100 scale), and both doc trees must name the same measured artifact and date. |
| [`dev_docs_drift_test`](../../tests/dev_docs_drift_test.rs) | A page under `docs/internals/` links to a path that no longer exists, names a `fn` that no longer exists, uses an absolute GitHub URL instead of a relative one, is not registered in `build-wiki.py`, or breaks a mermaid convention. It also builds the wiki and fails if any relative link survives into the output — the wiki is flat and has no repo tree, so such a link publishes dead. That check runs the generator rather than reading it: the version that only asserted `CODE_LINK_RE` appeared in the script passed while `](../bench/)` was shipping broken. |
| [`link_integrity_test`](../../tests/link_integrity_test.rs) | Any relative link or heading anchor in either doc tree does not resolve; Zola content uses a plain relative `.md` link that would render as a dead URL. On the wiki-source side the scan is the top-level `docs/*.md` plus `docs/internals/` — `docs/design/` and `docs/research/` are planning material outside the published journey and are deliberately not walked, though a link *into* them from a scanned page still has to resolve. A third scope covers the root community files (`README.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `MAINTAINERS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`), which neither doc tree walks — these are what GitHub renders in the sidebar, so a rename that broke their cross-references used to go unnoticed. |
| [`doc_example_coverage_test`](../../tests/doc_example_coverage_test.rs) | A user-facing CLI flag appears in fewer than two documented examples. A ratchet — the exemption list may only shrink. |
| [`flag_coverage_test`](../../tests/flag_coverage_test.rs) | A new long flag ships with no test referencing it. Also a ratchet: adding a test for a grandfathered flag fails until you remove it from the baseline list. |
| [`keybinding_drift_test`](../../tests/keybinding_drift_test.rs) | A controller handles a key that the F1 help never mentions. |
| [`config_wiring_test`](../../tests/config_wiring_test.rs) | A config key exists but is never read, or a CLI flag has no config fallback where its peers do. |
| [`feature_gate_test`](../../tests/feature_gate_test.rs) | A flag whose subsystem is not compiled in fails late or silently instead of fast and clearly. |
| [`api_guidelines_test`](../../tests/api_guidelines_test.rs) | A growth-prone public enum loses `#[non_exhaustive]`, or a shared store stops being `Debug`. |
| [`summary_consistency_test`](../../tests/summary_consistency_test.rs) | Two serializing surfaces disagree about a dialog or stream field. |
| [`wasm_exports_test`](../../tests/wasm_exports_test.rs) | The WASM binding loses an export the browser analyzer calls. |
| [`site_journey_test`](../../tests/site_journey_test.rs) / [`mockup_alignment_test`](../../tests/mockup_alignment_test.rs) | A website journey breaks, or a terminal mockup on the site drifts from real output. Also the homepage's advertised numbers: the binary-size ceiling, the glibc floor, the throughput tiles (which must quote a figure that appears on the benchmarks page they link to), and the automated-test count, which the template must read from the file `pages.yml` generates rather than state as a number. It holds the standards cards to a canonical table naming the code symbol behind every item, the field the program emits for every quality metric, and a citation in `docs/` and the built site mirror, one card per standard. It also holds the homepage's four MCP examples to the files [`gen-mcp-examples.sh`](../../demos/gen-mcp-examples.sh) generated, and holds each of those to the claim the surrounding copy makes about it. That covers the second half of `live binary -> website/data/mcp-examples/*.json -> index.html`; `demos/gen-mcp-examples.sh --check` covers the first and needs a built binary, so CI cannot run it. The homepage's voice-stack section must link exactly the guides in the "Your SIP server" and "Add to your voice stack" groups of the docs navigation, so a guide added to one reaches the other. |
| [`config_examples_test`](../../tests/config_examples_test.rs) | A config sample in the docs no longer parses. |
| [`doc_commands_run_test`](../../tests/doc_commands_run_test.rs) | A command shown in `docs/`, the README or a hand-written page under `website/content/` is one sipnab refuses. It extracts every `sipnab …` line from every shell block, including a fence indented under a list item, through the same CommonMark fence rule as [`scripts/lib_markdown.py`](../../scripts/lib_markdown.py) (it checks the two parsers agree on every page), and RUNS 447 of the 496 against a capture that ships with the repository, several at a time, each in a directory and a home of its own, failing on a usage error rather than on a non-zero exit -- plenty of documented commands exit non-zero for honest reasons. A device or root example runs with a device name that cannot exist substituted for the one the page names, so its flags still parse in full; a server example runs under a shared wall-clock bound, because clap refuses in milliseconds and a process still alive after it necessarily parsed its arguments. Only two kinds never run, and it names both: a shell program rather than one invocation, and a command that would exec something of its own or attach to the kernel. A command matching neither fails the test. It prints its own coverage, because the difference between "352 ran" and "3 ran, 380 skipped" is the difference between a gate and a decoration. |
| [`examples_run_test`](../../tests/examples_run_test.rs) | A program in `examples/` no longer runs the way its own comment says, or prints something other than the output the comment shows. It runs every `cargo run` command the comments document (12, across all seven programs), except one under `sudo`, and holds `docs/library.md`'s count of the programs to the directory. |
| [`release_surface_test`](../../tests/release_surface_test.rs) | A release adds a flag, MCP tool or REST route that no release note names, or a guide's Tested on names a sipnab release older than a flag its commands use. It reads the three lists at every release tag, with extractors it first holds to clap and the MCP router. |
| [`homepage_claim_truth_test`](../../tests/homepage_claim_truth_test.rs) | A claim the homepage states in PROSE stops being true: the MCP tool counts and their read-only split, which released builds carry the `bpf` feature, what the installer actually puts on a host, a capability the static musl build does not have, the filter language's field and operator counts, a TUI key the page names that nothing binds, and a CLI flag the page names that does not exist, plus the `unsafe` count and the safety claim resting on it — the page said "memory-safe by construction" beside 88 `unsafe` blocks and no `forbid(unsafe_code)`. `site_journey_test` gates the tiles; this gates the sentences, because the two disagreed on one page for months. |
| [`cookbook_recipes_test`](../../tests/cookbook_recipes_test.rs) | A command in [`docs/examples.md`](../../docs/examples.md) no longer runs or names a flag `--help` lacks; or a command it executes has no output golden in [`tests/cli/cookbook/`](../../tests/cli/cookbook) and no reason in the checker's `OUTPUT_UNPINNED` table; or a golden there is one no cookbook command produces. |
| [`support_selftest`](../../tests/support_selftest.rs) | The shared normalization helper changes behavior under the tests that depend on it. |
| [`released_port_scan_test`](../../tests/released_port_scan_test.rs) | A test under `tests/` binds a loopback port 0, reads the port, and releases the socket before using the number, which a test running alongside can take in between. |

The rule for all of them: **the gate is not the problem**.

- If `flag_coverage_test` fails, the flag needs a test.
- If `dev_docs_drift_test` fails, a page now lies.
- Adding an exemption is the last resort.
- Every exemption list in this repo works as a ratchet, so it cannot quietly grow.

## The client example programs

Three checks cover the programs under `clients/` that the user pages quote.

- `client_snippets_test` holds every `<!-- snippet: clients/... -->` block
  on `docs/rest-api.md`, `docs/client-examples.md`, the metrics and MCP pages
  and the hand-written [`website/content/docs/api-clients.md`](../../website/content/docs/api-clients.md) to the marked
  region of its program, byte for byte. It also requires
  [`scripts/smoke-clients.sh`](../../scripts/smoke-clients.sh) to run the site's whole clients, the capability
  examples and the operator tasks.
- `example_parity_test` holds the lifecycle table on
  `docs/client-examples.md` to the programs in `clients/`.
- [`scripts/smoke-clients.sh`](../../scripts/smoke-clients.sh) runs every program end to end on loopback,
  against sipnab servers replaying captures in the repository. CI runs it
  after the build step that builds the binaries and examples. Each program
  must print its exact output lines and must fail on a failure case: a wrong
  token, a missing call or customer, a capture with nothing to judge, or no
  TFPS.

What the script does that a reader of the user page does not need to:

- It waits for evidence, never a fixed sleep: `source_exhausted` in
  `/v1/stats` before it queries a replaying server, and `packets_admitted`
  in `/v1/hep/senders` before it reads the HEP roster. sipnab discards input
  it has not processed when it stops.
- TFPS bans by writing a pinned BPF map as root, which no CI runner allows.
  The ops server runs with `--tfps-ctl` naming
  [`clients/python/tests/fake_tfps_ctl.py`](../../clients/python/tests/fake_tfps_ctl.py), which answers in the documents
  `tfps_ctl --json` prints. [`clients/python/tests/test_fake_tfps_ctl.py`](../../clients/python/tests/test_fake_tfps_ctl.py)
  holds it to the fixtures pinned against the real binary. The script checks
  that the stand-in's block list holds the two banned addresses.
- `evidence_handoff.py` runs twice over one capture into two file roots, and
  the script requires the same output and byte-identical files. The absolute
  path each answer carries is the one difference, and the program prints it
  relative to its root. The README and manifest name the sipnab version, so
  the script compares two runs rather than pinning hashes.
- `agent_triage.py` runs over stdio and then over HTTP, against a server
  started on loopback port 0 with a signing key generated at run time and
  `--mcp-tools core`. The signed token must print the same lines as the stdio
  run. A token signed with another key, a token minted from the same key for
  the REST API, and a request with no token must each get `401`.
- `customer_export.py` reads three files cut from `sip-problem-call.pcap` the
  way a wrapped `tcpdump -C -W` ring leaves them, and `capinfos` and `tshark`
  read the export.
- The BPF half of `--uprobe-tls` needs root and a kernel with BTF, so no CI
  runner can run it. [`examples/tls_plaintext_records.rs`](../../examples/tls_plaintext_records.rs) runs the decode half
  on records laid out as the BPF program publishes them.

## The development loop

**Logging.** `SIPNAB_LOG` is a `tracing` `EnvFilter`.

- So it takes levels and per-module directives
  (`SIPNAB_LOG=debug`, `SIPNAB_LOG=sipnab::rtp=trace`).
- In TUI mode sipnab suppresses logging unless `SIPNAB_LOG` says otherwise.
  - The alternative is log lines painting over the interface.
- `-q` lowers the default in CLI mode.
- Configured by [`init_logging()`](../../src/app/bootstrap.rs).

**Benches.** `cargo bench --profile profiling`.

- Plain `cargo bench` *cannot build*.
  - The `cdylib` crate type needed for the WASM build forces
    `panic = "abort"` into the lib unit.
  - Bench units build with unwind.
  - So shared dependencies get built twice with incompatible panic strategies.
  - They fail to unify.
- The `profiling` profile is release codegen with `panic = "unwind"` and
  debug symbols kept.
  - That is also what callgrind wants.
- Baselines live in [`benches/BASELINES.md`](../../benches/BASELINES.md).

**nextest.** [`.config/nextest.toml`](../../.config/nextest.toml) defines three profiles:

- `default` (no retries, 30s slow timeout).
- `ci` (no retries, no fail-fast, immediate-final output).
- `e2e` (2 retries, 60s timeout) for the timing-sensitive tmux tests.

Worth knowing: **no workflow currently invokes nextest**.

- CI runs plain `cargo test`.
- The config is there for local use.
- It is also there for the day the e2e shim goes away.

**The docker lab.** [`harness/`](../../harness) is a docker-compose stack
for generating real traffic.

- It holds OpenSIPS, rtpengine and SIPp.
- `make up` in that directory builds and starts it.
- `make down` tears it down.

**WASM.** One pre-commit gate covers the browser analyzer.
It checks that [`website/static/wasm/sipnab.js`](../../website/static/wasm/sipnab.js)
still exports every function the site calls.

A second gate once demanded a freshly built bundle alongside any staged
[`src/wasm.rs`](../../src/wasm.rs).

- It no longer exists, nor does the binary it guarded.
- The published analyzer went eleven releases stale while that gate stayed green.
  - The reason: [`src/wasm.rs`](../../src/wasm.rs) had no commits in the window.
  - The interface held still while the implementation behind it moved.
- The Pages workflow builds the bundle at deploy time now.
  - So the build produces what ships, rather than the tree carrying it.
  - It cannot go stale.

**Feature matrices.** A green `cargo test --features full` is not proof.

- CI also builds reduced feature sets.
- Code behind `#[cfg(not(feature = ...))]` is invisible to the full build.
- For exactly this reason, the pre-push hook runs two checks before pushing:
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
  - The `fuzz` workspace check.

## Failure-path coverage

The tests and audits behind the operator [fault model](../fault-model.md). That
page says how sipnab behaves under each fault class. This section records what
pins each behavior.

### Parser panic surface

Two harnesses exercise every parser reachable from packet or file bytes:

- **Coverage-guided fuzzing**: [`fuzz/fuzz_targets/`](../../fuzz/fuzz_targets) (cargo-fuzz /
  libFuzzer).
  - The targets run weekly (and on demand) via [`.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`](../../.github/workflows/fuzz.yml).
  - Crash reproducers upload as artifacts.
- **Continuous fuzzing**: the same targets run under ClusterFuzzLite from
  [`.clusterfuzzlite/`](../../.clusterfuzzlite).
  - Batch fuzzing and corpus pruning run daily. A coverage report runs weekly.
  - The difference from the weekly run above is the corpus.
    It persists between runs instead of restarting from the tracked seeds.
    So what libFuzzer learns accumulates instead of starting over.
- **Always-on smoke fuzz**: [`tests/smoke_fuzz_test.rs`](../../tests/smoke_fuzz_test.rs) runs in
  `cargo test` (no nightly needed).
  - It runs ~40k random + structurally mutated inputs per entry point under `catch_unwind`.
  - It covers the same parser set **plus**:
    - the full link-layer decap chain (`parse_packet` across several link types),
    - the pcap file reader.
  - A caught panic fails the test. The offending input is hex-dumped for a repro seed.
  - Calling every fuzz entry point also compile-checks their signatures.
    So a target that drifts out of step with its parser breaks the test build.
    It does not drop out of the fuzz suite unnoticed.
  - Example: [`fuzz/fuzz_targets/sip_parser.rs`](../../fuzz/fuzz_targets/sip_parser.rs) had passed a `&str` transport
    argument where `parse_sip` takes `TransportProto`.
    The whole suite stopped compiling, with nothing in `cargo test` to say so.

The smoke layer is the regression floor. It found a UTF-8 char-boundary
panic in the TLS keylog hex decoder
([`src/capture/tls.rs`](../../src/capture/tls.rs)).
Nobody had ever run the committed fuzz target against that decoder.

- The decoder checked **byte**-length parity, then sliced `&hex[i..i+2]` as a `str`.
- So a multi-byte UTF-8 char (for example `€`, 3 bytes) split by the 2-char window panicked.
  The message was "byte index is not a char boundary".
- That was a remote DoS via a crafted `SSLKEYLOGFILE` line.
- The decoder now works on raw bytes with explicit nibble validation instead.
  Any non-ASCII or non-hex byte gives a clean parse error naming its offset.
- The regression test `decode_hex_multibyte_utf8_does_not_panic` and the corpus seeds in
  [`fuzz/corpus/keylog_line/`](../../fuzz/corpus/keylog_line) pin it there.

**Property tests**: [`tests/property_test.rs`](../../tests/property_test.rs) (proptest) asserts the
*semantic* invariants the fuzzers cannot:

- a SIP message built from generated fields parses back to those fields,
- SDP survives a build→parse→rebuild round trip,
- the filter DSL is a total function on arbitrary text (parse then evaluate never panic).

**Verified bounded in code** (confirmed by audit, exercised by
<!-- A list whose items carry their own parentheses and units. Semicolons are the
separator that keeps it readable -- the super-comma use Google's own guidance
keeps. Splitting on periods would turn one list into eight fragments. -->
<!-- vale Google.Semicolons = NO -->

fuzz): SIP header count (≤200) and fold size (≤8 KB); websocket payload
(≤64 KB); TLS record length (≤18432); IP/GRE encapsulation depth (≤5);
RTP CSRC / RTCP report counts (5-bit fields); all length-driven
<!-- vale Google.Semicolons = YES -->

`Vec::with_capacity` sites bounded by the actual slice.

- RTP/RTCP length-field arithmetic (`u16 * 4`) cannot overflow `usize`.
- Each multiply carries a bounds `ensure!` after it.

### Resource bounds

| Store | Bound proven by |
|-------|-----------------|
| `DialogStore` | [`tests/resource_bounds_test.rs`](../../tests/resource_bounds_test.rs) (50k unique Call-IDs, both modes, `len() ≤ cap` at every step) |
| `StreamStore` | same test (50k unique SSRCs) |
| per-dialog messages | `dialog_store.rs` unit tests |
| per-stream audio frames | `stream_store.rs` |
| IP/TCP reassembly | `reassembly.rs` |

### Capture, sink and concurrency audit

Audited, found sound (true-positive findings: none):

- **Capture file** ([`pcap_reader.rs`](../../src/capture/pcap_reader.rs)):
  - Magic/length/block-truncation all return clean errors.
  - Tests cover them (`too_short_file`, `invalid_magic`, `truncated_epb_block_no_panic`). The smoke fuzz also exercises them.
  - The FILE path implements the same exit-status rule as the live path. It did not always.
    - Reading a set deliberately continues past a truncated member and returns `Ok`.
    - So the join never saw it, and a truncated pcap exited 0 with a whole-looking report.
  - `ReadTally::report` in [`src/capture/file.rs`](../../src/capture/file.rs) is the one place both the single-threaded and `--cores` readers converge on.
    - It records the same `lost` predicate that decides its log severity into the run-integrity record in [`src/output/run_integrity.rs`](../../src/output/run_integrity.rs).
    - The exit-code sites and the `--json-dialogs`/`--report` markers read that record.
    - One place emits both the human sentence on stderr and the machine record. So they cannot disagree.
  - A `--plugin` that would not load is the same class and lands the same way
    (exit `1`, `plugins.failed` in the record).
  - The same record also carries idle compaction. Idle compaction deliberately does NOT move the exit status.
    A retention policy doing what you configured it to do is not a failed run.
- **Live loop** ([`capture/live.rs`](../../src/capture/live.rs)):
  - Device-open and BPF-compile failures return clean errors via the ready channel.
  - Receiver-dropped breaks cleanly.
  - A transient `recv()` error is fatal to the capture thread, and untested.
  - The thread ends by returning the error rather than panicking.
  - The exit status is the only place the partial-read distinction survives.
    Downgrade that join to a warning and exit 0, and an incomplete run reads exactly
    like a whole one to anything checking `$?`.
- **event_exec**: sipnab reaps every child, and a test covers the escaping.
- **Log/JSON sinks**:
  - `serde` escaping.
  - `\r\n` stripped from alert log values (log-injection guard, tested).
  - Writes use `?`, no `unwrap`.
- **Shutdown**:
  - Atomic-flag signal handlers ([`signals.rs`](../../src/signals.rs), tested).
  - `parking_lot` locks cannot poison.
  - Closed-channel sends checked.
- **`unsafe`**: libc and other FFI calls, with RAII/Drop-guarded fd ops.
  - Every block states its own soundness argument.
  - `Cargo.toml` sets clippy's `undocumented_unsafe_blocks` to `warn`.
  - Both the pre-push hook and CI run clippy with `-D warnings`.
    So a block with no adjacent `// SAFETY:` comment fails the build.

### Untested failure paths

- Live-capture **transient recv error**: needs a fault-injecting capture source.
- **Interface-down mid-capture**: funnels into the same fatal recv path.
- **Opus decode** ([`rtp/opus_decode.rs`](../../src/rtp/opus_decode.rs)) delegates to the external `libopus`.
  Its FFI input is length-checked. The codec itself is not fuzzed here.
- No disk-full test for the pcap/wav writers. Writes propagate `?`, so there is
  no panic, but no test covers the error path.

# Contributor walkthroughs

Seven ordered checklists for the changes people actually make.

- Each step names the test that fails if you skip it.
- Where no test enforces a step, it carries **(unenforced)**.
  - That is prose, and prose is what gets forgotten.
  - So those are the steps to be deliberate about.

Checking the enforcement claims here meant making the change and watching the
gate fail. More often than expected, it meant watching it pass.

Where the first draft of this page and reality disagreed, reality won:

- Adding a CLI flag does *not* trip `docs_drift_test`.
- The compiler turns away an MCP tool that holds a lock across an await
  before clippy gets a word in.
- **Three of the six checklists turned out to name gates that do not fire at all**
  for the change they sat beside.
  - Those steps now carry **(unenforced)**.

The pattern behind all three: a gate that hardcodes its subjects cannot see a *new* subject.

- Examples of hardcoded subjects:
  - Three flood scenarios.
  - Two output-flag behaviors.
  - Until it was rewritten to enumerate the directory, a list of schema filenames.
- Such a gate protects what exists from regressing.
- It does not notice an addition.
- Assume nothing enforces a new thing until you have watched it fail.

## Add a CLI flag

- Add the `#[arg]` field to `Cli` in [`cli.rs`](../../src/cli.rs), with a
  `help_heading` matching its group.
  - → [`cli_help_test`](../../tests/cli_help_test.rs) checks the grouping of the
    ~160-flag help output.
- Wire it wherever it takes effect.
  - Usually that is [`plan()`](../../src/app/bootstrap.rs).
  - So the flag becomes part of `RunPlan` rather than at the point of use.
- Give it a row in [`settings.rs`](../../src/settings.rs).
  - The row names the `[section] key` it shares with the config file.
    - It also names how the two combine
      (`Merge::Override`, `Either`, `Union` or `Off`).
  - Or the row names why it has no key
    (`Action`, `Input`, `Secret`, `PerRun`).
  - A standing setting gets a key, added
    to [`config.rs`](../../src/config.rs) beside its peers.
  - → `settings::tests::every_flag_has_exactly_one_row` **fails immediately**
    with `not classified: zzz-gate-probe`.
  - Once the row names a key, the two reference gates in the same module demand two things:
    - `docs/cli-reference.md` says `Config: [section] key`.
    - `docs/config-reference.md` names the flag.
  - `SIPNAB_SETTINGS_APPLY=1 cargo test --features full --lib settings` writes both.
    - Then `python3 scripts/build-site-pages.py` carries them to the site.
  - → [`config_wiring_test`](../../tests/config_wiring_test.rs) catches a config
    key that is never read.
- Add a test that references the flag by name.
  - Any test, anywhere under `tests/`, including a `.trycmd` golden.
  - → [`flag_coverage_test`](../../tests/flag_coverage_test.rs) **fails
    immediately** without one.
    - `zzz-gate-probe` in its message is the flag you just added.
- Document it in at least **two** examples across the docs.
  - → [`doc_example_coverage_test`](../../tests/doc_example_coverage_test.rs)
    fails with `--your-flag: 0 example(s)` until you do.
- Add a default-value case to
  [`cli_defaults_test`](../../tests/cli_defaults_test.rs).
  - **(unenforced — that test does not enumerate the CLI, so a missing case passes silently.)**

A config key with no flag goes in `settings.rs`'s `FILE_ONLY` list with its reason.

- Verified 2026-10-03:
  - A throwaway `zzz-gate-probe` flag failed `every_flag_has_exactly_one_row`.
  - A throwaway `[capture] zzz_probe_key` failed two checks:
    - `every_config_key_is_named_once` (`unclassified key`).
    - `every_config_key_has_a_row_naming_its_flags` (`no row in
      docs/config-reference.md`).

Verified: adding a throwaway `#[arg(long = "zzz-gate-probe")]` had these results.

- It failed `flag_coverage_test` and `doc_example_coverage_test`.
- `docs_drift_test`, `cli_defaults_test` and `config_wiring_test` all stayed green.
- `docs_drift_test` guards the *other* direction.
  - That is a flag named in the docs that the CLI does not have.

The two gates that do fire, in the order you meet them:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dev as you
    participant Cli as src/cli.rs
    participant FC as flag_coverage_test
    participant DE as doc_example_coverage_test
    participant CI

    Dev->>Cli: add #[arg] field
    Dev->>FC: cargo test
    FC-->>Dev: FAIL — flag referenced by no test
    Dev->>Dev: add a test or a .trycmd golden
    Dev->>DE: cargo test
    DE-->>Dev: FAIL — 0 example(s) in the docs
    Dev->>Dev: document it twice
    Dev->>CI: push
    Note over CI: both gates are ratchets — the exemption lists may only shrink
```

## Add a TUI view

Model it on the newest one, `StreamLossMap`.
Its commit touched exactly these places.

- Add the variant to `View` in [`state.rs`](../../src/tui/state.rs).
- Add the renderer.
  - It is a module beside [`loss_map.rs`](../../src/tui/loss_map.rs).
  - Register it in [`render/mod.rs`](../../src/tui/render/mod.rs).
- Keep the computation out of the renderer.
  - `StreamLossMap`'s binning core lives in [`rtp/loss_map.rs`](../../src/rtp/loss_map.rs)
    with its own unit tests.
  - So the view logic is testable without a terminal.
- Add the controller in [`controllers/`](../../src/tui/controllers).
  - Route it in [`controllers/mod.rs`](../../src/tui/controllers/mod.rs).
- Add the key that opens it, in whatever view it opens *from*.
- Document that key in `HELP_TEXT` in [`help.rs`](../../src/tui/help.rs) **and**
  in [`docs/keybindings.md`](../keybindings.md).
  - → [`keybinding_drift_test`](../../tests/keybinding_drift_test.rs) fails with
    `these handled KeyCode::Char keys are neither in the F1 help nor
    allow-listed`.
  - It names both the view and the character.
- Add snapshot coverage in
  [`tui_snapshot_test`](../../tests/tui_snapshot_test.rs).
  - At minimum, the populated case and the empty/degenerate case.
- Mirror the keybinding into [`website/content/docs/keybindings.md`](../../website/content/docs/keybindings.md).
  - **(unenforced for a new key — the mirroring obligation is a convention. See
    CONTRIBUTING.)**

Verified: binding `KeyCode::Char('Y')` in the call-list controller without
touching the help failed two assertions in `keybinding_drift_test`.

## Add an MCP tool

- Add the handler to [`server.rs`](../../src/mcp/server.rs) under the
  `#[tool_router]` impl.
  - Give it a `#[tool(name = …, description = …)]` attribute.
- Write the description as a **statement of what the tool returns**.
  - Never instruct the model to "trust", "verify", "act on" or "ensure" anything about
    the content.
  - That is the prompt-injection rule (D22 in
    [`../design/implementation-plan-phases-8-10.md`](../design/implementation-plan-phases-8-10.md)).
  - **(Enforced by [`tests/mcp_tool_descriptions_test.rs`](../../tests/mcp_tool_descriptions_test.rs),
    which fails on any of those four words in a tool description.)**
  - **(Corrected 2026-08-05.)**
    - This used to call the rule unenforced.
    - It also used to claim `server.rs` cited a `scripts/check-tool-descriptions.sh`
      that does not exist.
    - Both halves are now wrong.
      - `server.rs` no longer carries the citation.
      - The rule shipped as a Rust test rather than the shell script the plan named.
    - That test also carries `every_cited_script_exists`.
      - It fails if the dangling citation ever comes back.
    - It now scans every tracked `.rs` file whole, not the first 40 lines of one.
      - The reason: the narrow version asserted nothing once the citation went away.
- Take the store guard, project what you need into owned data, **drop the
  guard**, and only then `.await`.
- Bound the response with [`resolve_limit_with_cap()`](../../src/mcp/shape.rs).
  - Pass the caller's `limit` and the server's `row_cap`.
  - Also bound it with the body-bytes cap (`--mcp-max-body-bytes` moves it).
  - A tool that pages with a cursor also takes `max_response_bytes`.
    - It passes its serialized page, after any `fields` projection,
      through `SipnabMcp::fit_to_budget`.
    - It passes the cursor that resumes after each row.
    - So the whole response stays inside
      `--mcp-max-response-bytes` ([`budget.rs`](../../src/mcp/budget.rs)).
  - **Not `resolve_limit()`.**
    - That one takes no ceiling.
    - So a tool wired to it silently ignores `--mcp-max-rows`.
    - The operator sets a limit and the tool does not honor it.
    - `shape.rs` says as much at the definition.
      - It is "kept for callers with no configured ceiling".
      - The server is not one of them.
    - This step used to name the wrong function.
      - That is how a recipe written for the reader who does not yet know
        manufactures the very defect it exists to prevent.
- Add an end-to-end case to [`mcp_stdio_test`](../../tests/mcp_stdio_test.rs).
  - For HTTP-visible tools, also add one to [`mcp_http_test`](../../tests/mcp_http_test.rs).

The step that drops the guard is not a style preference.

- The rmcp router requires each handler's future to be `Send`.
- A `parking_lot` guard held across an await makes it non-`Send`.
- So the build fails on the `#[tool]` attribute with *"future cannot
  be sent between threads safely"*.
  - That happens before `clippy::await_holding_lock` (denied at
    the workspace level) is even consulted.
- There are two independent mechanisms. The stricter one is the compiler.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Client as MCP client
    participant Tool as tool handler
    participant DS as DialogStore
    participant Shape as shape.rs

    Client->>Tool: call_tool
    Tool->>DS: read()
    DS-->>Tool: guard
    Tool->>Tool: project into owned summaries
    Tool->>DS: drop(guard)
    Note over Tool: the guard is gone — the future is Send again
    Tool->>Shape: resolve_limit_with_cap, body cap
    Shape-->>Tool: bounded payload
    Tool-->>Client: CallToolResult
```

## Add a REST route

- Add the handler to [`src/output/api.rs`](../../src/output/api.rs), register it in `build_router`, and
  give it a `#[utoipa::path]` annotation.
- Give the route a `### METHOD /path` heading in `docs/rest-api.md`, and
  document every query parameter the annotation declares.
  - **(Enforced by `openapi_contract_test`.)** It compares three lists: the
    published document, the live router, and the headings in
    `docs/rest-api.md`. It fails when any two disagree, and when the
    reference never mentions a parameter the document declares.
- Regenerate the published document (next section).
  - **(Enforced by `openapi_contract_test`, which fails on a stale
    [`website/static/openapi.json`](../../website/static/openapi.json).)**
- If the route answers a question an MCP tool also answers, return the same
  shape from the same code. The REST reference states which tool matches each
  route.
  - **(Enforced for listed answers and fields by `surface_parity_test`.)**
    It fails when an answer in its `CAPTURE_ANSWERS` table has an MCP tool
    and no route or the reverse, and when a quality metric, caveat counter or
    provenance field reaches one API and not the other. A new answer is
    checked only once someone adds it to that table **(unenforced)**.
- A route that reads a request body inherits the 1 MiB
  `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` cap from the router's `DefaultBodyLimit` layer. A
  larger body answers `413`, and a body that does not parse answers `400`.
  Do not add a second limit.

The REST reference shares these derivations with other surfaces. Change the
shared code, not a copy:

| REST route | Shared with | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/report` | `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}` | `generate_call_report` in [`src/output/call_report.rs`](../../src/output/call_report.rs) delegates JSON to the one dialog serializer |
| `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/correlated` | MCP `find_correlated` | `CorrelationResult::strategy_and_gap` in [`src/sip/dialog_store.rs`](../../src/sip/dialog_store.rs) |
| `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/tree` | MCP `get_call_tree` | `DialogStore::correlation_tree` in [`src/sip/dialog_store.rs`](../../src/sip/dialog_store.rs) |
| `POST /v1/vcon/validate` | MCP `validate_vcon` | `vcon_schema::validate` in [`src/output/vcon_schema.rs`](../../src/output/vcon_schema.rs) |
| `POST /v1/vcon/analyze` | MCP `analyze_vcon` | `vcon_analysis::analyze_container` in [`src/output/vcon_analysis.rs`](../../src/output/vcon_analysis.rs) |
| `GET /v1/capabilities` | MCP `server_capabilities`, `--version` | `compiled_features` in [`src/cli.rs`](../../src/cli.rs), read from `cfg!`; the `libpcap` block is `pcap_lib_version` asked at runtime |

The `/v1/dialogs` list rows are the compact `DialogSummary` projection shared
with MCP and TUI save. That is why they carry `from_user`/`to_user` while the
single-dialog document carries `from`/`to`.

The live-audio WebSocket closes with code 1002 on a client frame longer than
`MAX_CLIENT_FRAME` (4096 bytes) in [`src/output/websocket.rs`](../../src/output/websocket.rs). A client sends
only control frames, which [RFC 6455](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455.html) caps at 125 bytes.

### Regenerate the OpenAPI document

A test step generates [`website/static/openapi.json`](../../website/static/openapi.json). Nobody writes it by hand.
`openapi_contract_test` derives it from the `#[utoipa::path]` annotations on
the handlers in [`src/output/api.rs`](../../src/output/api.rs), and splices in the shared JSON Schemas
under `tests/schemas/` rather than describing those response bodies twice.
Regenerate it after changing a handler:

```bash
SIPNAB_BLESS_OPENAPI=1 cargo test --features full --test openapi_contract_test
```

- The test file compiles only with the `api`, `vcon` and `native` features.
  A build without `vcon` registers no `/v1/dialogs/{call_id}/vcon` and would
  generate a different document, so the published document describes the full
  build.
- [`scripts/check-generated-inputs-staged.py`](../../scripts/check-generated-inputs-staged.py), run by the pre-commit hook,
  refuses a commit that stages the document while one of its inputs has
  changes that are not staged.
- `info.version` is `1`, the `/v1` path version, not the release version. A
  patch release that changes no endpoint must not invalidate a document a
  client already cached.

## Add a security detector

- Add the module under [`src/security/`](../../src/security).
  - Put it beside [`scanner_detect.rs`](../../src/security/scanner_detect.rs) or
    [`reg_flood.rs`](../../src/security/reg_flood.rs).
  - Export it from [`security/mod.rs`](../../src/security/mod.rs).
- Keep detector state bounded and attacker-keyed maps capped.
  - A detector is by definition fed hostile input.
  - **(unenforced — [`resource_bounds_test`](../../tests/resource_bounds_test.rs)
    is three hand-written scenarios over `DialogStore` and `RtpStream`. It has no
    way to discover your module.)**
- Run its check from `run_detectors` in
  [`security/detectors.rs`](../../src/security/detectors.rs).
  - That returns the finding as an `Effect` for the batch loop to file.
  - Emit through the alert engine in
    [`alerting.rs`](../../src/security/alerting.rs) rather than printing.
  - So every sink (CLI, TUI, `fail2ban`, MCP `security_findings`) gets it.
  - A new rule name also belongs in two places:
    - `SECURITY_FINDING_KINDS` ([`mcp/server.rs`](../../src/mcp/server.rs)).
      - This is the vocabulary `security_findings.kinds` accepts.
      - A finding filed under a name missing from it is one no caller can filter for.
    - `DetectionEngines::armed_kinds` ([`batch.rs`](../../src/app/batch.rs)).
      - This is what tells an agent the run armed the detector at all.
  - **(enforced — `security_findings_kinds_match_the_names_the_detectors_file_under`
    reads the `kind:` literals in `batch.rs` and fails on the difference.)**
- Add regression coverage to [`security_test`](../../tests/security_test.rs).
  - Include the false-positive case.
  - A detector that fires on normal traffic is worse than no detector.
  - **(unenforced — nothing requires a new detector to have a
    test.)**

Verified: a new [`src/security/`](../../src/security/) module held an uncapped `HashMap<IpAddr, u64>`.
`mod.rs` exported it.
It left `resource_bounds_test` at 3/3 and `security_test` at 38/38.
Both steps above are real obligations with no gate behind them.
That is exactly why this page writes them down.

- If it can *transmit* anything, it must be opt-in.
  - It must respect the HEP-origin restriction (SN-01).
  - HEP-sourced packets are ineligible for active response without `--hep-allow-kill`.

## Add an output format

- Project through [`output/model.rs`](../../src/output/model.rs).
  - Do not build a bespoke JSON object for a dialog or a stream.
  - **(unenforced for a new surface —
    [`summary_consistency_test`](../../tests/summary_consistency_test.rs) pins
    the three surfaces that already exist, CLI/API/MCP, against
    `DialogSummary`/`StreamSummary`. A fourth writer is invisible to it.)**
- Add the writer beside [`json.rs`](../../src/output/json.rs) /
  [`cli_print.rs`](../../src/output/cli_print.rs).
  - Emit through [`sink.rs`](../../src/output/sink.rs).
- If it is machine-readable, add or extend a schema in
  [`tests/schemas/`](../../tests/schemas).
  - There is no registration step.
  - The `all_schemas_compile` case in
    [`json_schema_test`](../../tests/json_schema_test.rs) enumerates the directory.
  - So a new file becomes a validator the moment it lands.
  - A malformed one fails there.
  - What is still on you is *live-output* validation.
    - That means proving the surface actually emits what the schema describes.
- Add behavior coverage to
  [`output_behavior_test`](../../tests/output_behavior_test.rs).
  - **(unenforced — it is two tests about `--json-pretty` and `--call-report` exit codes.)**

History, and the reason the schema step now reads that way.
A deliberately malformed `zzz_gate_probe.schema.json` was once dropped into
[`tests/schemas/`](../../tests/schemas/).
It left `json_schema_test` at 6 passed, 0 failed.
The test walked a hardcoded list of four filenames and never opened the file.
That experiment is what motivated the switch to directory enumeration.
The test's own doc comment records it.
The model, writer and behavior-coverage steps are still convention with no gate behind them.

- Document it in [`docs/output-formats.md`](../output-formats.md).
  - Mirror it into the website page.
  - The flag that selects it then owes the CLI-flag checklist above.
- A new finding kind or evidence count label in
  [`src/analysis.rs`](../../src/analysis.rs) changes two published contracts.
  - A test holds each one to the table.
  - Give the variant its arm in `ordinal` and `meta` (or `as_str` and
    `description` for a `CountLabel`). The compiler insists.
  - Give it its place in `ALL`, which a `const` assertion checks.
  - Then add it to
    [`tests/schemas/capture_analysis.schema.json`](../../tests/schemas/capture_analysis.schema.json).
    - `json_schema_test` fails until the `kind` enum or the `counts` properties
      name it.
  - Last, the YANG module.
    - Users already hold its current revision, so do not bless over it.
    - Add an entry to `REVISIONS` in
      [`src/analysis/yang.rs`](../../src/analysis/yang.rs) with the day's date.
    - Point `MODULE_TEXT`'s `include_str!` at the new file name.
    - Run `SIPNAB_BLESS_YANG=1 cargo test --features full --test yang_module_test`.
    - Keep the previous file under `yang/` beside the new one.
    - [`yang_module_test`](../../tests/yang_module_test.rs) fails until the
      committed module names the kind.
    - [`scripts/check-yang.py`](../../scripts/check-yang.py) runs
      `pyang --check-update-from` over the pair.

## Add a fuzz target

- Add `fuzz/fuzz_targets/<name>.rs` calling one parser entry point on
  `&[u8]`.
- Register the `[[bin]]` in [`fuzz/Cargo.toml`](../../fuzz/Cargo.toml).
  - **(unenforced, and this is the trap.)**
    - An unregistered file under `fuzz_targets/` is not a broken build.
      It is an invisible one.
    - Cargo never compiles it.
    - So `fuzz-check` and the pre-push `cd fuzz && cargo check` both pass.
    - Your target silently never runs.
- Seed [`fuzz/corpus/`](../../fuzz/corpus) with at least one real input.
  - **(unenforced — despite the name,
    [`fuzz_corpus_replay`](../../tests/fuzz_corpus_replay.rs) never opens
    [`fuzz/corpus/`](../../fuzz/corpus/).)**
    - It has no filesystem access at all.
    - It drives the parsers with an adversarial seed set and a mutation sweep
      defined in the file itself.
- Add the same entry point to
  [`smoke_fuzz_test`](../../tests/smoke_fuzz_test.rs).
  - Coverage-guided fuzzing needs nightly and runs weekly.
  - The smoke floor runs in every `cargo test`.
  - It is what actually catches the regression.
- When a target finds a crash, commit the reproducer into the corpus in the
  same change as the fix.
  - The seeding step's replay does not read the corpus.
  - So add the input to `smoke_fuzz_test` too, if you want it replayed on
    every `cargo test`.

Verified: an unregistered `fuzz/fuzz_targets/zzz_gate_probe.rs` contained a
hard compile error.

- It left `cd fuzz && cargo check` at exit 0.
- Registering the same file made the same error fail the build with exit 101.
- The gate only ever sees registered targets.

<!-- source: docs/internals/build-ci-release.md -->

# Build, CI and release

This page covers four things:

- What compiles.
- What gates a merge.
- What runs on a tag.
- Which of those you can safely ignore.

## Features

`Cargo.toml`'s `[features]` table has fourteen entries.

- The thirteen named features below.
- Plus `default`, which is `native, tui, audio, metrics`.

`full` is everything except `wasm` and `bpf`.
That is not the whole story of what ships.

`bpf` sits outside `full` for one reason.

- Building it needs a nightly toolchain and `bpf-linker` for the kernel object.
- This project cannot demand either of a contributor.

The RELEASE has both.

- `release.yml` builds the four `*-linux-gnu` matrix
  entries with `--features full,bpf`.
- It installs the two tools.
- It sets `SIPNAB_BPF_REQUIRED=1`.
  - So a runner missing either tool fails the build.
  - It does not publish a binary that advertises the feature and refuses at runtime.

The musl and macOS artifacts do NOT carry it, for two different reasons.

- musl:
  - `bpf` costs +589,952 bytes.
  - The published 0.5.117 x86_64 musl binary is 12,252,424 bytes.
  - Under the 12 MB ceiling that left 330,488 bytes of headroom, and it did not fit.
  - The ceiling `release.yml` enforces has risen several times since.
    `binary_size_ceiling_mb` in [`website/config.toml`](../../website/config.toml) holds the current figure.
    So it would fit now.
  - musl still excludes it.
    What a static artifact carries is a decision about the artifact, not about bytes.
    Raising a ceiling does not make that decision.
- macOS:
  - `Cargo.toml` declares `aya`
    under `[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]`.
  - So the feature would compile to nothing while `--version` claimed it.

On those binaries `--uprobe-backend bpf` still refuses.

- `sipnab --version` is how you tell which build you hold.
- It lists every compiled feature, `bpf` and `plugins` included.

| Feature | Implies | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `native` | — | Everything that cannot compile to WASM: libpcap capture, clap, the pcap file writer, the tracing subscriber. Most other features imply it. |
| `tui` | `native` | The ratatui/crossterm terminal UI. |
| `tls` | — | TLS/SRTP decryption: `ring`, `rustls`, keylog parsing, and `zeroize` for key material. **Does not imply `native`** — decryption is useful in the WASM analyzer too. |
| `hep` | `native` | HEP/EEP capture source, with HMAC auth. |
| `metrics` | `native` | The standalone Prometheus `/metrics` listener. Raw TCP and threads, deliberately independent of `api` — you can ship metrics without the axum stack. |
| `audio` | — | The `sipnab-audio` plugin loader for TUI playback. **Does not imply `native`**; it is a `dlopen` of a separate cdylib. |
| `api` | `native` | The axum REST API. |
| `mcp` | `native` | The MCP server over stdio. |
| `mcp-http` | `mcp` + `api` | Streamable-HTTP MCP transport; depends on `api` so both share one axum stack rather than duplicating it. |
| `plugins` | `native` | The `wasmi` WASM plugin host. **Non-default on purpose** — someone who does not want an interpreter inside their capture tool does not get one. See [`../design/wasm-plugin-api.md`](../design/wasm-plugin-api.md), which measures the cost at +1.56 MB and 15 crates. |
| `wasm` | — | The browser analyzer bindings. Lib-only: its test and bin targets are meaningless on the host. |
| `vcon` | `native` | vCon export: one observed dialog as an unsigned OBSERVER conversation container. **Non-default on purpose** — the stock build gains no conversation-container writer at all. It sits INSIDE `full`, so the pre-commit hook's `cargo test --features full` covers it. sipnab writes the container as an observer: nothing signed, a party `name` only from a `From` or `To` display name and never vouched for, and no `url` — retained audio travels INLINE as base64url or not at all, under a measured size budget the emitter refuses out loud. |
| `bpf` | `native` | The eBPF uprobe backend — the only one that can report the peer address a TLS session went out to, because it pairs each write with its `tcp_sendmsg`. **Outside `full`**: the kernel half needs nightly and `bpf-linker`. Shipped on the four `*-linux-gnu` release artifacts, not on musl or macOS. |
| `full` | everything but `wasm` and `bpf` | What the pre-commit hook and most local testing use. The released gnu binaries add `bpf` on top. |

The implications that surprise people:

- **`tls` and `audio` do not pull in `native`**.
- `mcp-http` pulls in *both* `mcp` and `api`.

So a green `--features full` says nothing about whether `--features tls` alone
compiles.
That is exactly why CI has a feature matrix.

## The eighteen workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | push, PR | The merge gate. See below. |
| `cert-expiry.yml` | daily at 07:10 UTC, and on changes to itself | Reads the EDGE and the ORIGIN certificates for sipnab.com and fails with three weeks to spare. Both, because the public name resolves to the CDN: on 2026-09-11 the edge certificate was healthy with 85 days left while the origin had expired and every visitor got a 526. It also refuses a CNAME that disagrees with `base_url`, which is what had been dropping the certificate on every deploy |
| `quality.yml` | push to main, PR, weekly cron (Wednesdays 04:23 UTC) + manual | Line coverage (`cargo-llvm-cov`), clippy SARIF upload, and the prose gates below on push and PR. Branch coverage (nightly) runs on the schedule, where it is the only job, and on a manual run, alongside the rest. Not required by `ci-success`. |
| `codeql.yml` | push to main, PR, weekly cron (Tuesdays 02:34 UTC) | GitHub's static analysis. |
| `fuzz.yml` | weekly cron (Mondays 05:17 UTC) + manual | Coverage-guided `cargo-fuzz` runs; crash reproducers upload as artifacts. |
| `clusterfuzzlite.yml` | daily (batch 02:23 UTC, pruning 05:23 UTC), weekly (coverage Sundays 06:23 UTC) + manual | Continuous fuzzing with a corpus that survives between runs, which `fuzz.yml` cannot do: batch fuzzing grows it, pruning keeps it minimal, and the coverage job reports which code it reaches. Builds in the OSS-Fuzz Rust builder image from `.clusterfuzzlite/`, which compiles the targets the way ClusterFuzzLite runs them. No pull-request fuzzing: without continuous builds on every push it would report pre-existing crashes as though the change introduced them. |
| `docker.yml` | push to main, `v*` tags | Builds and pushes the image to GHCR with sigstore provenance. |
| `pages.yml` | push to main (path-filtered) | Builds and deploys the Zola website, with the homepage test count taken from CI's run of the same commit. |
| `scorecard.yml` | push to main, weekly cron (Mondays 07:20 UTC), branch-protection change | OpenSSF Scorecard posture analysis → Security tab. Report-only. |
| `wiki-sync.yml` | push to main (path-filtered) | Regenerates the wiki from `docs/` via [`scripts/build-wiki.py`](../../scripts/build-wiki.py). |
| `release.yml` | `v*` tags | The release. See below. |
| `sanitizers.yml` | weekly cron (Tuesdays 06:11 UTC) + manual + on its own path | ThreadSanitizer over the threaded integration suites. Nightly as a tool, not as the toolchain. |
| `memcheck.yml` | weekly cron (Wednesdays 07:23 UTC) + manual + on its own path | Runs sipnab under Valgrind across its offline, archive, HEP, MCP and REST paths, built with `--cfg sipnab_tsan` so it allocates through the C library's heap, the only heap Valgrind sees. A definitely or indirectly lost block, or an invalid read, write or free, fails the job ([`scripts/memcheck-verdict.py`](../../scripts/memcheck-verdict.py)), and so does a log with no leak summary. Valgrind must first report a probe program's one known 4,096-byte leak, or the job fails. Runs on the local runners. |
| `self-hosted-smoke.yml` | manual (`workflow_dispatch`) | Proves the self-hosted runner can build sipnab before any production job runs on it. Fires on no automatic event, so no PR can execute on the box. |
| `pr-text.yml` | `pull_request_target`: PR opened, edited, reopened or pushed to | Checks the text a pull request publishes for the lab's private identities and for AI attribution with [`scripts/check-message-identity.sh`](../../scripts/check-message-identity.sh), the script the `commit-msg` hook runs. The `Commit messages and PR title name no private identity` job reads the title, the branch name and every commit message in the pull request's range, which is what a merge puts on `main`, and fails on a finding. The `PR description names no private identity (advisory)` job reads the description, which stays on the pull request page, and reports a finding as a warning without failing. Both jobs check out the base branch (no checkout names a ref, which Scorecard's Dangerous-Workflow check would report), so main's workflow, script and test judge the pull request, and the job fetches the pull request's commits from `refs/pull/N/head` as data and never checks them out or runs them; the fetched head must equal the event's head SHA. `contents: read` at the workflow level and no cache, because a `pull_request_target` run otherwise holds a write token and a cache it saves is restorable on main. Every value from the event reaches the shell only through `env:`. The pull request that added the workflow was not checked by it, because main had no `pr-text.yml` yet. Not required by `ci-success`. |
| `osv-scanner.yml` | push to main, PR, weekly cron (Wednesdays 05:41 UTC) + manual | Vulnerability matching against osv.dev for EVERY lockfile, not just the crate graph. Not redundant with `cargo audit`: that reads Cargo.lock and RustSec only, so advisories against the Actions pins, the Dockerfiles or the fuzz workspace are invisible to it. It also queries a service rather than keeping a local advisory clone, so it does not share the stale-cache failure that broke every `cargo audit` for a day on 2026-08-09. |
| `bench.yml` | daily cron (03:29 UTC) + manual | 4-core offline reconstruction against the baseline in [`bench/baseline.json`](../../bench/baseline.json), failing below 80% of it. Exists because a 40% regression shipped in four releases with every test green. Nightly and wide-banded on purpose: the reference host also serves CI, so a per-push wall-clock gate would measure contention. |
| `reproducible.yml` | weekly cron (Thursdays 04:37 UTC), manual, and PRs touching the build's inputs | Builds the aarch64 gnu release binary twice from one commit, in two directories with two `$CARGO_HOME`s, on the self-hosted runner, and fails unless the stripped binaries and symbol files are identical. See [Reproducible builds](#reproducible-builds). |

### ThreadSanitizer

`sanitizers.yml` runs the threaded integration suites under
`-Zsanitizer=thread`, weekly.
It exists because nothing else in the suite can see a data race.

- The tests exercise the capture thread, the channel, and the
  processing thread.
- But to `cargo test`, a test that passes and a test that raced are
  indistinguishable.

The borrow checker does not help here either.

- It stops at `unsafe`.
- Most of this crate's 135 `unsafe` blocks are libc FFI.
- They concentrate in privilege dropping ([`privilege.rs`](../../src/privilege.rs)
  and [`process_isolation.rs`](../../src/process_isolation.rs)) and capture setup.
- Recount with `grep -rc 'unsafe {' src/` rather than trusting that figure.
  This sentence said 49 until 2026-09-06, when the tree held 92.

Three things about it are deliberate.

**Nightly is a tool, not the toolchain.**

- `-Zsanitizer` is nightly-only, and so is `cargo-fuzz`.
- Both run in their own workflow.
  The release build stays on the pinned stable version.
- Moving the build to nightly would break three things:
  - the toolchain pin
  - the MSRV promise
  - the reproducibility of a released binary

**`-Zbuild-std` is mandatory, not optional.**

- Without it, the standard library is not rebuilt with instrumentation.
- Then TSan sees `std`'s synchronization as opaque.
- It reports the channel itself as a race.
- That noise is what gets a race detector switched off.

**The scope is a sample, and the workflow says so.**

- Five suites run:
  - the REST API and its token path
  - HEP
  - MCP stdio
  - the CLI behavior tests
- Nothing finds a race in a path outside that list.
- Add the suite rather than assuming coverage.

[`ops/tsan/suppressions.txt`](../../ops/tsan/suppressions.txt) silences libpcap, libasound and the dynamic loader.
TSan cannot instrument them.

- Each entry carries the reason it is not a real race.
- An unexplained suppression turns a race detector into a race ignorer.

**The sanitizer build drops mimalloc.**

- `RUSTFLAGS` carries `--cfg sipnab_tsan`.
- [`src/main.rs`](../../src/main.rs) skips its `#[global_allocator]` under that cfg.
- Why:
  - mimalloc is C compiled by the `cc` crate.
  - So `-Zsanitizer=thread` does not instrument it.
  - TSan sees neither its alloc/free (no shadow reset on a recycled block)
    nor its internal cross-thread synchronization.
  - Every block handed from one thread to another reads as a data race.
- The 2026-07-29 run reported exactly that.
  - Its stacks named `read` and `Vec::append_elements_unreserved`.
  - They had no allocator frame anywhere.
  - So a suppression could not have matched it.
- `docs/design/backlog.md` records the bisect.
- The shipped binary keeps mimalloc.
  Only the sanitizer build differs.

**The verdict reads every process, and classifies.**

The step greps rather than trusting the exit code.
TSan can report a finding and still exit 0 when the test passes.
Two things make that grep mean something.

- `log_path` gives each process its own `tsan.<pid>`.
  - The suites spawn the `sipnab` binary and consume its stderr.
  - Before this, a report from a child reached the log only if some
    test happened to print the child's stderr into an assertion message.
  - The first run's "0 races" meant "nothing printed".
- The verdict names the finding it actually matched.
  - It does not call everything a data race.
  - An earlier draft would have reported a thread leak as one.

`thread leak` is in the fatal set.

- It was briefly written off as expected.
  The reasoning: sipnab exits fail-fast paths through `std::process::exit`,
  which joins nothing.
- That had it backwards.
  - `bootstrap::launch` spawns the capture thread *before* the readiness hand-shake,
    the chroot, and the privilege drop.
  - So every failure from there on abandoned a thread still holding an open
    capture source.
  - `sipnab -I /nonexistent.pcap`, a mistyped filename, was enough to do it.
- Those paths go through `capture::stop_and_join`.
  - It sets the shutdown flag, drops the receiver, and joins.
- The suites report zero leaks.
  The fatal classification is what keeps it that way.

A missing `__tsan_init` in the built binary fails the job outright.
Otherwise a build that quietly lost its instrumentation would report a clean run
forever.

All of that lives in [`ops/tsan/verdict.sh`](../../ops/tsan/verdict.sh), not inline in the workflow.

- [`ops/tsan/test-verdict.sh`](../../ops/tsan/test-verdict.sh) sits beside it.
- A `tsan-verdict` job in `ci.yml` runs it on every push.

The inline version had to move because it was wrong in the direction nobody checks.

- `run:` blocks execute under `bash -e -o pipefail`.
- So its bare `grep … | while read` warning loop exited 1
  on a tree with **no** findings.
- That killed the step before it could report.
- The job failed silently when clean and passed while a thread leak was present.

The instrumentation guard had the mirror of it.

- `grep -q` closed the pipe on a still-writing `nm`.
- It read SIGPIPE as "not instrumented".

Nothing could have caught either without running the logic against a fixture.
That is the whole argument for it being a script.

### The prose gates

`quality.yml`'s `Docs` job runs three tools over `docs/`, [`website/content/`](../../website/content/) and
`README.md`:

- Vale with the Google style package
- codespell
- lychee twice:
  - once over the Markdown
  - once over the site Zola builds from it

The built-site pass matters.

- It is the only place the generated pages get checked.
- It cannot run on this project's own aarch64 hardware, where no Zola binary exists.

`.vale.ini` carries the whole policy, and reading it beats re-deriving it.
It records:

- which rules fail the build
- which ones sit disabled, with the alert count each produced
- which ones a measurement rejected, because the advice did not survive contact
  with this corpus

Five rules fail the build today.
Four more sit off, with their reasoning recorded rather than left for the next reader to rediscover.

**This repo pins the style package to an exact release.**

- `Packages = Google` resolves through the registry to `releases/latest/download`.
- CI runs `vale sync` on every job.
- So that spelling makes every prose gate depend on
  whatever upstream published last.
- A local styles tree is only as fresh as the last manual sync.
  So a green local run says nothing about CI.

Google v0.7.0 landed 2026-07-30 13:43 UTC and rewrote one rule's regex.

- A gate measured and enabled against the older package reported 0 alerts locally and 35 in CI.
- main went red.

`vale_style_package_is_pinned_to_a_release` holds the pin.
To upgrade:

- Change the version.
- Run `vale sync`.
- Re-run Vale and read the diff in alert counts before committing.

### Coverage, and running it before CI does

The `Quality` workflow's coverage job runs `cargo llvm-cov`.
It enforces a line floor with `--fail-under-lines`.

- The floor sits just under the measured figure.
  So it ratchets against decline without failing on noise.
- The workflow comment carries the measurement and the commit it came from.
- Raise it when the real number rises.
- Never lower it to make a build pass.

[`scripts/coverage.sh`](../../scripts/coverage.sh) reproduces that job locally, before a push:

Collect, summarize and enforce the floor:

```bash
scripts/coverage.sh
```

Report the last collection without re-running it:

```bash
scripts/coverage.sh --report
```

It **reads the floor and the scope out of the workflow** rather than repeating them.

- The scope is the workflow-level `COVERAGE_TEST_SKIPS` and
  `COVERAGE_IGNORE_REGEX` in `quality.yml`.
  The workflow states it once, and every `cargo llvm-cov` call there uses it.
- Two copies of a threshold is how a gate and its local rehearsal come to disagree.
  - The rehearsal is the one that gets trusted, because it is the one that answered first.
- [`tests/coverage_gate_test.rs`](../../tests/coverage_gate_test.rs) fails in three cases:
  - the script grows its own floor
  - the two skip different tests
  - someone walks the floor backwards

It is deliberately **not** in the pre-push hook.

- An instrumented build plus the full suite is 30-60 minutes.
  The hook is already around fifteen.
- A gate nobody waits for is a gate people bypass.
- And the claim that one exists is what stops someone adding a real check later.
- A test asserts it stays out.

The two `--skip` flags are technical rather than preferences.

- `cli_goldens` spawns the instrumented binary as 13 parallel child processes.
  They collide on the llvm-cov merge-pool `.profraw`.
- `wasm_plugin_` shells out to a wasm32 build.
  wasm32 ships no `profiler_builtins`, so the nested build fails `E0463`.

Both run in full under the plain `cargo test`.
So the run loses only their coverage contribution.
That is why this total falls short of the whole suite by design.

### Branch coverage

The line job cannot count branches.

- `cargo llvm-cov --branch` needs rustc's `-Z coverage-options=branch`.
- Only nightly accepts that.
- The line gate stays on the pinned stable toolchain.

So `quality.yml` has a second job, `coverage-branch`.

- It runs weekly (Wednesdays 04:23 UTC) and on a manual run only.
- It uses the same nightly pin `fuzz.yml` and `sanitizers.yml` use.
- It collects under the same scope as the line job.
- It uploads to Codecov under the flag `branch`, beside the line report rather than over it.

`cargo llvm-cov` has `--fail-under-lines`, `-regions` and `-functions` but no branch floor.
[`scripts/branch-coverage.py`](../../scripts/branch-coverage.py) reads the
`--json --summary-only` export instead.

- It fails a report that holds no branches at all.
  That means `--branch` never took effect.
- It enforces `--floor` when the job passes one.
- The job passes none yet.
  - The first measurement was a local aarch64 run on 2026-09-30 over the job's scope.
  - It was **77.46%** (13221 of 17069 branches), under OpenSSF Gold's 80%.
- Once the real number clears 80, set the floor just under it.
  This is the same ratchet as the line floor.

### What actually gates a merge

`ci-success` requires every other job in `ci.yml` — thirteen of them: **`check`,
`install-sh`, `deb-package`, `rpm-packaging`, `homebrew-formula`,
`tsan-verdict`, `bench-scripts`, `features`, `crate-package`, `audit`,
`fuzz-check`, `code-scanning-clean`, `symbol-split`**.

`ci_success_gates_every_job` in
[`site_journey_test`](../../tests/site_journey_test.rs) holds the list to that.

- It once named only the four below.
- The comment above it claimed "every other job" at the time.
- So `install-sh` and `deb-package` could both fail with the
  one required check on main still green.

The rest of this section describes four of them.
Their contents are worth spelling out.

- **`check`** (per-OS matrix):
  - `cargo build --all-features`
  - `cargo test
    --all-features`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features --workspace`
  - plus the `--ignored` PTY TUI end-to-end tests
  - On Linux it also compiles the Python clients under `clients/python/`.
    It runs `pytest` over their tests and `scripts/tests`.
- **`features`**: `cargo check --no-default-features --features X --tests`
  across fifteen feature sets.
  - The sets: each of `native`, `tls`, `api`, `mcp`, `hep`,
    `metrics`, then `tls,api`, `native,tui,audio`, `native,tui,tls,hep,api`,
    `native,hep,api,mcp,mcp-http`, `bpf`, `vcon`, `audio`, `plugins`, and `wasm`
